Decided by 0.22, lost on the bench

Week 3 in Interstellar came down to the smallest margin of the season and the biggest unforced error. Dobbin on ur Rob till im Worthy edged Waddle on ma Johnson 141.98 to 141.76, a 0.22-point decision that Luke will replay all week, because Harold Fannin Jr. scored 24.1 on his bench while Kaleb Johnson scored 2.6 in his lineup.

Elsewhere, Quinn put up the week's high of 148.1 to take the top spot in the power rankings, Thomas hung a 49.16-point beating on Daniel for the season's biggest blowout, and Christian moved to 3-0 behind another monster day from Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

The league left 195.48 points on benches this week. Two games were decided by them. Tucker and Daniel are both 0-3, and De'Von Achane turned a 20.2-point projection into 1.7.

Margin 0.22 · Bench cost the game

Fannin Jr. rots on the bench as Waddle on ma Johnson loses by 0.22

Dobbin on ur Rob till im WorthyPatrick · 141.98
by 0.22
TRU
Waddle on ma JohnsonLuke · 141.76

Dobbin on ur Rob till im Worthy beat Waddle on ma Johnson 141.98 to 141.76, a 0.22-point margin that stands as the closest game of the season. Bijan Robinson ran 29 times for 194 yards and two touchdowns for 37.3 points, Brock Bowers added 29.6 on 10 catches, and the waiver-wire Vikings D/ST chipped in 19 with six sacks and two picks.

Luke got everything he could want from his stars: Jahmyr Gibbs scored 41.4 with three touchdowns, Garrett Wilson added 28.7 and Kenneth Walker III scored 21.3. None of it mattered, because his own bench had enough points to win. Harold Fannin Jr. caught two touchdowns for 24.1 on the bench while freshly claimed Kaleb Johnson started and managed 2.6 on four carries.

Luke left 40.5 points on the bench in a game he lost by 0.22. Patrick wasn't flawless either, starting Trevor Lawrence (19.78) over Bo Nix (24.14) and getting 3.7 from Tetairoa McMillan, but he gets to call it a learning experience with a win attached.

Gibbs scored 41.4. Fannin scored 24.1. Only one of them was allowed to help.

Rushing to Retirement beat China's Greatest Fear 148.1 to 121.48, a 26.62-point win built on balance. Tyler Shough threw four touchdowns for 23.8, Davante Adams went for 137 yards and 22.7, and Derrick Henry punched in two scores for 21.9.

Nani got 33.28 from the undrafted Brock Purdy, who threw four touchdowns, plus 22.2 from CeeDee Lamb. But the Bengals D/ST, picked up off free agency this week, gave up 30 and scored 0, and Christian Watson's 22.6 sat on the bench.

Quinn's lineup wasn't spotless: the 49ers D/ST also posted a 0 and Michael Wilson scored 25.9 on his bench. It didn't matter. When you score 148.1, you can afford to leave a little on the table.

She Burrowed her fingers in Pep crushed Little young black children 137.28 to 88.12, a 49.16-point margin that is the biggest blowout of the season. Drake London caught nine passes for 194 yards and 30.4 points, Joe Burrow threw three touchdowns for 22.58, and Harrison Mevis went 4-for-4 on field goals for 17.9.

Daniel was projected for 135.7 and finished with the week's low of 88.12. De'Von Achane got three carries for 17 yards and 1.7 points against a 20.2 projection, and Jalen Hurts managed 12.62 with no passing touchdowns.

Ja'Marr Chase did his part with 24.8, but this one was over early. Thomas left only 1.5 points on his bench all day.

Njigba Please beat malik n 126.8 to 91.98, winning by 34.82 to stay the league's only unbeaten team. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 10 balls for 128 yards and two touchdowns for 37.36, Matthew Golden added 23 and Lamar Jackson contributed 20.44.

Christian's only blemish was new kicker Trey Smack, who went 0-for-1 on field goals for 1 point. Tee Higgins scored 21 for John, and Bhayshul Tuten's 17 on the bench wouldn't have saved him.

Kyren Williams (21.8), James Cook III (21.4) and Matthew Stafford (20.9, with 390 passing yards) all delivered. Carson left 25.4 on his own bench, including Juwan Johnson's 23.3, and still won going away.

Draft watch

The top of the draft paid off. Jahmyr Gibbs, the first overall pick, led all scorers with 41.4 for Luke, and No. 2 pick Bijan Robinson scored 37.3 for Patrick. Christian's sixth overall pick, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, added 37.36, and Thomas's 16th overall selection, Drake London, posted 30.4. The best quarterback of the week, Brock Purdy at 33.28, went undrafted. The late-round steal is George Kittle, taken 74th overall by Carson, who scored 26.2 with two touchdowns. The early-round bust is De'Von Achane: drafted 10th overall by China's Greatest Fear, now on Little young black children, and good for 1.7 points this week.

Trends

  • The bench is winning games The league left 195.48 points on benches this week, and two games went to the team whose opponent sat the difference. Luke left 40.5 and lost by 0.22; Tucker left 39 and his best possible lineup of 131.7 would have beaten Carson.
  • The two best teams have one win each Rushing to Retirement and Waddle on ma Johnson have the league's top two averages at 146.4 and 143.8 and have beaten their projections every week. They're both 1-1-1, thanks in part to their 154.62 tie with each other in Week 2.
  • John is living on borrowed points malik n is 2-1 with a 97.8 average, a 4-23 all-play record and zero weeks above projection. His scores have dropped from 103.46 to 97.94 to 91.98, and Quinn is next.
  • Defense was a coin flip The Bengals D/ST and 49ers D/ST each scored 0, and the Eagles D/ST finished at -1. Meanwhile Patrick's waiver-claim Vikings D/ST put up 19 with six sacks and won him a game decided by 0.22.
